title: Consolidated billing in AWS Organizations

kcs.statement: Consolidated billing in AWS Organizations gives the management account one bill for all member accounts at no extra charge, while still itemizing each account's charges.
Consolidated billing combines usage across accounts for tiered pricing, so ten accounts storing 10 TB each in S3 are priced as 100 TB and reach cheaper tiers sooner.

Reserved Instance and Savings Plans discounts are shared across all accounts in the organization by default, so an unused RI in one account can discount matching usage in another; the management account can turn sharing off.

problem_ideas: Three accounts each send 4 TB out a month and the first price tier ends at 10 TB: predict how many TB are billed at the lower tier with consolidated billing.
Account A bought an RI it no longer uses and account B runs a matching instance: who gets the discount?
A finance team wants one invoice for 40 accounts: which feature, and what does it cost?
A subsidiary must keep its RI discounts to itself: what does the management account change?
Spot the false statement: 'Consolidated billing merges all accounts into one account.'
Which account is responsible for paying the consolidated bill?
